[2407] Need for change

[2408] The overall goal of personnel policy is to have a highly motivated personnel corps with the competence to carry out the Armed Forces' tasks

[2409] The tasks, structure and organisation of the armed forces have changed drastically since the end of the Cold War

[2410] However, personnel management and the Armed Forces' education system have not been sufficiently adapted to these changes

[2411] The lack of reforms has had unfortunate consequences, both in terms of operability, personnel safety, management of operations and cost-effectiveness

[2412] In order to achieve a flexible personnel structure in times when the Armed Forces' needs are constantly evolving, a set of reforms is therefore proposed that will provide flexible solutions adapted to future challenges

[2413] The main elements of the proposed reforms, both in terms of the command system and the practice of conscription, are a follow-up to signals given in Recommendation

[2414] S. no. 342 (2000–2001), cf. St.prp

[2415] No. 45 (2000–2001), and in Recommendation No

[2416] S. no. 232 (2001–2002), cf. St.prp

[2417] no. 55 (2001–2002), as well as in the Chief of Defence's military technical report

[2418] In some areas, it has been necessary to assess the Chief of Defence's proposal in light of the personnel policy in the State as a whole, and in light of the experiences gained through the downsizing in recent years

[2419] The government supports the main features and direction of the Chief of Defence's recommendations, but also puts forward a number of related proposals to supplement them

[2420] The proposed reforms are necessary for four reasons

[2421] Firstly, the Armed Forces' competence needs are increasingly characterised by the introduction of advanced technology, and by more complex and demanding operations at home and abroad

[2422] To increase the operational efficiency of the Armed Forces' departments, and to help improve safety during exercises and operations, it is therefore necessary to increase the level of experience among younger commanders

[2423] The Armed Forces lack an education scheme and a career system that ensures sufficient continuity, experience and competence at lower levels

[2424] To be appointed to the Armed Forces today, one must either have a military academy or a civilian education at military academy level

[2425] This education is primarily aimed at positions at middle and senior management levels in the Armed Forces, and leads to employment as a professional officer

[2426] Officers advance relatively quickly out of lower-level positions, which is partly a natural consequence of the type of competence that military academy education is aimed at, and partly a consequence of the fact that there are relatively too many higher-level positions in the Armed Forces

[2427] The latter is handled by reducing the number of positions in the strategic management, the command structure and foreign positions, cf. chapter

[2428] These factors mean that positions at the lower levels of the Armed Forces organization are occupied by the youngest commanders, who will rarely have gained the experience that is highly desirable for this type of demanding position

[2429] Secondly, changes in the structure and organization of the Armed Forces have changed the requirements for the age composition among commanders

[2430] The future Defence Force will have a greater need for younger commanders in the departments, for tasks related to force production, preparedness and operations

[2431] The quantitative need for senior commanders, which was previously dimensioned by tasks related to staff functions such as planning and management of a large mobilization defense, has, however, been greatly reduced

[2432] The Armed Forces are unable to achieve an age structure adapted to this need with the current command system

[2433] The Armed Forces have a relatively large proportion of professional officers aged 30–

[2434] Since the current scheme for professional officers has extended job protection, and there is very little turnover among professional officers, the large proportion in this age group will shift further

[2435] The current command system, with permanent appointments directly after the military academy, is therefore inappropriate for meeting the needs of the Armed Forces, because it leads to a relatively equal number of commanding officers at each age level, and means that the age profile in the officer corps is governed by the need for a large number of younger officers at lower levels in the Defence organisation

[2436] This leads to significant overstaffing at higher levels in the organization

[2437] Without structural changes, these problems will continue to develop

[2438] As the Chief of Defence points out in his military-technical report, there is a need for a more flexible command system, where the right education and service experience are ensured at all levels in the organisation

[2439] The Armed Forces must be given better opportunities to adapt the volume of personnel at the different age levels 2003–2004 St.prop

[2440] The further modernization of the Armed Forces in the period 2005–2008 ne

[2441] An adjustment of the personnel volume is particularly necessary in the transition between service in operational departments and staff service, a shift that usually occurs when officers are in their mid-30s

[2442] For the third, it is necessary to ensure the Armed Forces stable and predictable access to personnel for all types of operations

[2443] The Armed Forces' new tasks require departments and units with high quality, responsiveness and deployability

[2444] To ensure synergies in the use of the Armed Forces' departments, it is important that the personnel can, as a general rule, be used for both national and all types of international tasks

[2445] The command corps must be available for both types of tasks in order to achieve the goal of available departments that are trained together, and have high quality and responsiveness

[2446] The command corps as a whole must acquire the important expertise that service in foreign operations provides, a competence that is crucial for the further transformation and development of the Armed Forces

[2447] It is also important that the burden of participation in foreign operations is distributed fairly across the entire command corps, not least to create the conditions for a predictable and good family life

[2448] In connection with the processing of the Recommendation

[2449] cf. St. meld

[2450] No. 38 (1998–1999), the Storting expressed support for introducing a system with an obligation to order, similar to the systems that were then introduced in Denmark, among others, and instructed the government to investigate the matter further and return to the Storting with a concrete proposal

[2451] see chapter

[2452] The Norwegian Armed Forces are currently in a situation where the voluntary principle of participation in foreign operations means that commanders can say no to one of the Norwegian Armed Forces' core tasks

[2453] Participation in such operations will, however, be a prerequisite for commanders and officers who have chosen the Armed Forces as a career path

[2454] Most people will still seek to be recruited through volunteering, and the obligation to order will be a safety valve to ensure that the Armed Forces have the necessary expertise in this regard

[2455] the individual assignments and to prevent individual groups or individuals from blocking political decisions

[2456] The premises for the practice of the duty to order should be fair distribution of the burden and that family considerations are taken into account

[2457] Fourth, it is important that conscription ensures that the Armed Forces have access to the most motivated and most suitable young people

[2458] Conscription is a pillar of the Norwegian Armed Forces, and helps to anchor the Armed Forces in Norwegian society

[2459] At the same time, it is most effective to base the practice of military duty on the needs of the Armed Forces, and ensure that the Armed Forces recruit personnel for the operational structure

[2460] The Armed Forces' need for expertise and personnel for operations abroad and at home means that the practice of conscription must be adjusted to meet these challenges

[2461] Below are outlined the main features of the changes proposed in the personnel area

[2462] As a result of some of the proposed changes and measures, the government will submit a proposal for a new Act on Personnel in the Armed Forces in the current session of the Storting

[2463] This applies to the proposals for the obligation to order international operations and the introduction of a new category of commander (department commander), both of which require legislative amendments

[2464] Recruitment will be crucial for the new Armed Forces to be able to carry out their tasks in a satisfactory manner

[2465] It is a goal for the Armed Forces to recruit the most motivated and best suited of both genders for the Armed Forces' diverse activities

[2466] The quality of personnel shall be ensured by ensuring that the Armed Forces are, and are actively marketed as, an exciting, varied and challenging workplace, as well as through selection and competition

[2467] It is particularly important to utilize the Armed Forces' departments and educational institutions in marketing the opportunities the Armed Forces can offer

[2468] The session will be developed to become a central recruitment and selection tool

[2469] Emphasis should be placed on correct classification and distribution, so that dropout during the service is as low as possible

[2470] Furthermore, it is a goal that there is a short period of time between the session and the call

[2471] Because the answer is concerned with recruiting women

[2472] To achieve this, the government proposes that all women be summoned to the session – without attendance being required by law

[2473] Status-raising measures for conscripts will be an important element in recruitment for, and motivation for, initial service

[2474] It is important that the new command system is presented as attractive in order to ensure good recruitment to all categories of command and officer positions

[2475] Recruitment to the officer training schools shall be ensured by allowing young people to apply for officer training schools prior to being called up for initial service, in the same way as in the current system

[2476] This will also be important for recruiting women

[2477] The modernized command schools and war academies will also be able to recruit from conscripts who are in their first year of service

[2478] An early and preliminary selection of relevant candidates will be carried out, so that motivation is maintained

[2479] For the new category of department commanders, i.e. personnel with at least a command school (cf. chapter 6.4.1), bonus schemes will be included, based on the St.prop

[2480] No. 42 2003–

[2481] The further modernization of the Armed Forces in the period 2005–2008 increased the length of service, limited upwards to a maximum of two years' salary upon resignation

[2482] An exciting, varied and challenging service, good management training and management experience, as well as a solid professional platform through systematic continuing education, in addition to the aforementioned bonus schemes, will contribute to good recruitment for this group of commanders

[2483] In addition, the department commander scheme will reach large groups who are not motivated for a longer, theoretical education, but who still want to work in the Armed Forces

[2484] This will increase the Armed Forces' recruitment area, and provide a significantly better offer to this group of young people

[2485] The professional officers, i.e. personnel with a military academy or equivalent education, will receive a salary during their training, broad leadership experience, and good prospects for permanent employment and challenging service in the Defence Forces

[2486] They should first and foremost be given competence as military leaders

[2487] The career officers will receive a civilian-recognized bachelor's degree and the opportunity for a master's degree, primarily within military subjects, which can also be built on in the civilian education system

[2488] Professional officers are experienced as being competitive in the labor market, by virtue of their expertise and military leadership experience

[2489] These conditions will ensure continued good recruitment of professional officers to the Armed Forces

[2490] Conscription is – and will continue to be – a pillar of the Norwegian Armed Forces

[2491] Conscription ensures that the Armed Forces have access to the most suitable and motivated young people, and is therefore very important for recruitment purposes

[2492] It also contributes to large parts of the population having a relationship with the Armed Forces, thereby anchoring the Armed Forces in Norwegian society

[2493] The fact that the Armed Forces' tasks, alignment and organization have changed over recent years does not alter this

[2494] Although the quantitative need for personnel, including conscripts, has been reduced, the qualitative need is higher than ever

[2495] Because conscription is so important to the Armed Forces, those who serve their first term must experience it as positive, educational and meaningful

[2496] Not least, it is important that conscripts feel that they are needed in the Armed Forces organization

[2497] In his military-technical report, the Chief of Defence has recommended that conscription be continued in a differentiated and flexible system, with initial service, an apprenticeship scheme, contract service and recruitment schemes adapted to the tasks and organisation of the Armed Forces

[2498] The following points must be given special emphasis regarding the practice of military service

[2499] – The operational needs of the Armed Forces must be the guiding factor for the number of conscripts

[2500] An increase in the number of conscripts beyond the Armed Forces' needs will correspondingly reduce the framework that can be used to meet operational needs

[2501] Such a development would weaken the status of conscription

[2502] – The initial service must be meaningful to the individual

[2503] – Session and recruitment become more important for correct selection

[2504] — Initial service in the Army, Navy, Air Force and operational joint institutions shall normally be 12 months and for HV a minimum of 4 months (3 calls per year) to provide the individual with a proper education

[2505] – A significant proportion of conscripts must be motivated during their initial service to sign contracts for service in the operational structure, including service in foreign operations

[2506] – The initial service may be part of an apprenticeship scheme or longer technical vocational schools/equivalent, where the service period is longer than 12 months

[2507] – Status-raising measures should be an important element in recruitment and motivation for first-time service, and conscripts should be well-off financially in a good way

[2508] – During initial service, the Armed Forces shall actively recruit officers and enlisted personnel

[2509] Adult education will be maintained at approximately the same level as today for the individual soldier

[2510] The course activities are being further developed in line with the crew's needs for vocational and study-related training

[2511] Conscripts serving their first military service shall continue to be Adult Education's primary group

[2512] In addition, the recruits must have good training opportunities throughout the contract period

[2513] This requires close cooperation between the Armed Forces' distance learning and Adult Education

[2514] During 2004, the Ministry of Defence will look into the possibility of merging these services, to make the offer more cost-effective and comprehensive from a user perspective

[2515] Size of the call-up force

[2516] Over the past few years, broad political acceptance has been established that the needs of the Armed Forces must govern the sizing of the conscription force

[2517] Such practice ensures satisfactory

[2518] staffing of the operational structure, while at the same time 2003–2004 St.prop

[2519] The further modernization of the Armed Forces in the period 2005–2008 ensures that those serving their first term receive meaningful service

[2520] It is important that those who carry out the initial service feel that they are needed in the organization, that the service enables them to solve the operational tasks they are assigned in an efficient and safe manner, and that the initial service provides status in society

[2521] At the same time, they must be compensated well

[2522] The possibilities for creating such a service are greatest if the Armed Forces' needs are the basis for the practice of conscription, because all conscripts will then perform tasks

[2523] The Armed Forces are actually required to solve this problem, because the Armed Forces will be of higher quality, and because both the Armed Forces and the first-time service will thus have higher social legitimacy

[2524] If the number of conscripts is increased beyond the actual needs of the defense, significant resources will have to be allocated to educating and training this personnel

[2525] Calculations show that this amounts to approximately NOK 390 million per 1,000 conscripted man-years, without this adding to defense capability

[2526] These are significant resources, which should rather be used to strengthen the Defence's real operational capability

[2527] At the same time, resources should be deployed to create a meaningful service, and those conscripts who serve for 12 months should be compensated with a significantly higher discharge allowance

[2528] The session will be developed to become a better recruitment and selection tool

[2529] It must be ensured that there is a short period of time between the session and the call-up, to avoid drop-outs among the young people the Armed Forces wish to recruit

[2530] Internet solutions should be used to ensure good advance information and for submitting self-declarations

[2531] Further measures to streamline the review process are under consideration

[2532] The government does not want to introduce mandatory attendance at sessions for women, partly because women are not subject to military service and therefore there are no legal or sanctioning means that can be used to ensure attendance at sessions

[2533] The government will therefore focus on positive measures, and emphasis will be placed on making the session a positive meeting with and answer for both women and men

[2534] It is therefore proposed that all women be invited to attend the session

[2535] Women will be contacted by the Armed Forces in the same way as the male population

[2536] Information should be provided about the good opportunities that service in the Armed Forces provides for further education and career opportunities

[2537] In this way, women and men will have approximately equal opportunities to receive information about Forsvaret in general and the educational schemes in particular, even though participation for women will be voluntary

[2544] The service supplement is increased in line with the annual salary settlements

[2546] This work will be carried out in consultation with the Ministry of Education and Research

[2547] It is planned to increase the proportion of conscripts, as this is necessary to increase the usability, responsiveness and quality of the Armed Forces' operational departments

[2548] Recruitment, signing of contracts and allocation to preparatory service are implemented during the initial service

[2557] New command system

[2558] The Chief of Defence has recommended several changes to the current command system

[2559] Below is an explanation of the government's proposal for a new command structure, which is mainly based on the Chief of Defence's proposal

[2560] Introduction of a new category of commander

[2561] Department Commanders In order to increase the Armed Forces' ability to carry out its tasks by solving the challenges associated with the need for specialized expertise and experience at lower levels in the organization, as well as the problems associated with the overproduction of older officers, it is proposed to introduce a corps of department commanders with limited long-term appointments

[2562] The department commander shall be given basic command training based on the command schools, and subsequent specialization according to the needs of the branches of defense

[2563] The commissioned officer will receive salary during further education

[2564] Education and the service pattern are structured so that the department commander, in collaboration with senior commanders, gains solid experience in lower-level positions in the Armed Forces

[2565] The increased experience base will increase the operational efficiency of the Armed Forces' departments, and at the same time contribute to improving safety during exercises and operations

[2566] The commander shall be given an education that enables them to exercise leadership in line with the expectations and values of both society and the Armed Forces

[2567] To achieve an appropriate age structure in the Armed Forces, this category should be appointed with a shorter employment relationship, but otherwise given the same rights and obligations as professional officers

[2568] The department commander is therefore normally given a permanent position until the age of

[2569] From the Armed Forces' side, it could be desirable for the employment relationship to have a longer duration

[2570] However, the age limit has been set at 35 years to ensure that this commander, who would not be given the opportunity to serve in the Armed Forces until retirement age anyway, ends his service in the Armed Forces at an age where he still has good civilian career opportunities

[2571] Employment until the age of 35 will also provide the employer with predictability

[2572] This enables long-term competence building in specialized and limited areas, while at the same time giving employees the opportunity for career planning and predictability for themselves and their families

[2573] In line with the Chief of Defence's recommendation, this command should occupy positions in the rank range from sergeant to lieutenant

[2574] Promotion to ensign and lieutenant is granted by the commander competing for a permanent position with a higher rank

[2575] To further facilitate the transition to a career outside the Armed Forces, an establishment and training bonus is being introduced at the end of service, capped at two years' salary

[2576] The department commander may be offered a professional position based on the needs of the Armed Forces

[2577] This applies especially to personnel who have expertise that the Armed Forces wishes to retain, and where the nature of the service does not require that one be under 35 years of age

[2578] It will be important that those who are suitable for such employment are identified early and informed about this in order to meet the personnel's needs for planning their further careers and family life

[2579] Many of the positions at the lower levels in the Norwegian Defence Organisation are currently filled by officers who have graduated from a military academy, because this is the only possibility of permanent employment

[2580] Many of these positions will in the future be filled by department commanders, due to the competency needs outlined above

[2594] Job security for professional officers

[2595] The Storting has decided to reduce the number of man-years in the Armed Forces by 5,000 by the end of 2005, compared to the situation in September

[2596] The proposal shows the need for further significant reductions in certain job categories into the next period

[2597] At the same time, professional officers today have absolute protection against dismissal, based on the nature of the business

[2598] In a sector that will also have to continuously adapt to changing framework conditions in the future, such a lack of flexibility is a formidable challenge

[2599] Today's extraordinary dismissal protection means that professional officers must resign voluntarily

[2600] This imposes enormous expenses on the Armed Forces in the form of very expensive severance packages

[2601] When the Armed Forces had achieved a reduction of approximately 2,000 man-years of the adopted reduction target of 5,000 man-years, NOK 2.63 billion had been spent on measures to stimulate turnover (including approximately NOK 500 million for civilian employees

[2602] The job security also places a strong limitation on the Armed Forces' ability to assess which expertise should be retained in the organization, because the Armed Forces – in order to achieve the downsizing goals – is under pressure to grant severance packages to those who are willing to leave

[2603] Another consequence of the professional officers' dismissal protection is that redundant personnel can increase their salaries right up to retirement age, without having relevant work duties

[2604] The government believes that the current severance pay scheme for professional officers is very generous and significantly better than what is found elsewhere in public or private enterprises

[2605] In addition to a set of financial instruments, the Armed Forces have established an organization to help redundant personnel transfer to other work outside the Armed Forces

[2606] While the pace of downsizing was satisfactory in 2001 and 2002, it has virtually come to a standstill

[2607] The Government will consider harmonizing the extraordinary job protection for professional officers with the job protection for civil servants in the state in general, if it proves necessary to ensure that the set downsizing targets are achieved

[2608] However, such harmonization is not proposed in this bill, or in the proposal for a new law on personnel in the Armed Forces, which is being put forward in a separate parliamentary bill

[2655] Order to international service

[2656] Today, participation in foreign operations is primarily based on voluntariness (NATO Article 5 operations excepted), but with the possibility of ordering commanders who began military school training after the Peace Service Act came into force on 1 January 1999, if sufficient participation cannot be achieved through voluntariness

[2657] The presentation of a proposal to expand the obligation to issue orders to international operations is a follow-up to the Defence Committee's signals in Recommendation

[2658] P. No. 152 (1999–

[2659] No. 38 (1998–

[2660] “The committee emphasizes that sufficient quality, quantity and predictability in personnel access are an absolute prerequisite for the Norwegian Defence Force to be able to contribute effectively internationally

[2661] The committee points out that participation in international operations is now an integrated part of the Armed Forces' ongoing tasks and that Norway has undertaken specific obligations in this regard

[2662] In the committee’s opinion, questions can be raised about the reasonableness of people who are professionally employed in the Armed Forces being able to refuse to carry out assignments that are an integral part of the Armed Forces' ongoing tasks and that Norway has committed to carrying out through international agreements

[2663] The committee believes that a command system for commanders, based on experiences from Denmark, should be considered for introduction and submitted to the Storting as a separate matter as soon as possible

[2664] In this context, the committee would like to point out that participation in international operations can still be sought on a voluntary basis, but that there should be general access to orders for professional employees in the Armed Forces

[2665] In this context, the committee would like to point out that it will take far too long before the provisions on orders in the current Peace Service Act have practical effect

[2666] In an era where there are fluid transitions between national and international security, between peace, crisis and war, and between Article 5 situations in NATO and other situations, the current system is not appropriate

[2667] With the exception of Poland, the Czech Republic, Portugal and Norway, all current NATO member states have a duty to commission officers

[2668] The Armed Forces need predictable access to personnel for all overseas operations, and want to 2003–2004 St.prop

[2669] The further modernization of the Armed Forces in the period 2005–2008 distribute this task, and not least the competence building this provides, as fairly as possible across the entire command corps, as described in chapter

[2670] A duty to order will also strengthen the ability to use the same personnel setup for the entire range of tasks, nationally and internationally

[2671] Previously, the Armed Forces recruited personnel, on a voluntary basis, from a large national mobilization force and set up smaller ad hoc units for use in international peacekeeping operations

[2672] Of an army that comprised 13 brigades and approximately 150,000 personnel, one battalion was continuously recruited, and under 1,000 people, primarily for UN operations, for example in Lebanon

[2673] Because the future Defence Force will be smaller, and operations abroad are a core task for the Defence Force, continuing such a practice will provide very little flexibility

[2674] It is most efficient and appropriate to use the same units nationally and internationally, which makes it necessary to ensure satisfactory access to the same personnel

[2675] It is also essential that the Armed Forces can manage the selection of personnel for such service based on competence and suitability, in addition to the need for fair rotation and reduced burden on individuals and groups, as well as their families

[2676] Recruitment based on volunteerism will continue to be the main rule, but the obligation to order is being introduced as a safety valve, in order to be able to implement political decisions in the government and the Storting

[2677] The duty to command will also contribute to commanders and officers considering operations outside Norway as a natural part of their profession, and as a consequence of their choice of profession

[2678] In accordance with the Chief of Defence's recommendation, it is therefore proposed to legislate the duty to give orders for all commanders and those categories of civilian personnel who are crucial to the operational efficiency of departments

[2679] As a result of the new arrangement, a general obligation to order all operations, national and international, will be part of the individual's employment relationship with the Armed Forces

[2680] The statutory duty to order is introduced for all officers, including those who are already employed, to ensure fairness and equal burden in the officer corps

[2681] Today's arrangements, with special standby contracts for limited periods and types of operations, will then cease for continuously serving commanders

[2682] For civilians and enlisted personnel, the statutory duty to order will only apply to those who are hired after the law comes into force

[2683] The obligation to order for civilians who were employed before the law came into force will have to be included in the individual's employment contract

[2684] The Reserve Command constitutes an important resource for overseas operations

[2685] For this category, the scheme with time-limited contingency contracts will be continued

[2686] Arrangements must also be introduced that ensure stable access to private personnel to the operational structure

[2687] The Government assumes that the obligation to order should be practiced as flexibly as possible

[2688] It is important not to place excessive burdens on individuals and groups of individuals and their families

[2689] That is precisely why it is important that everyone contributes and shares in the tasks

[2690] As the Chief of Defence has pointed out

[2691] Those serving in units on standby for operations will be able to be ordered to all operations and training activities at home and abroad together with their unit

[2692] Such departments will in principle rotate between preparedness, training, exercises, operations and retraining after the mission is completed

[2693] Furthermore, the need for personnel will vary between the different degree levels

[2694] There will thus be a natural accrual of the individual's service as a result of these circumstances

[2695] An application may be made for a postponement of the order, based on important health, welfare, family or social reasons

[2696] In addition, efforts should be made to comply with a policy that ensures a minimum of one year at home between different operations

[2697] However, there will be a big difference between having a basic obligation to command as a safety valve, then striving for flexible practice, and continuing the current principle of voluntary service for commanders

[2698] The duty to order will ensure that the Armed Forces can recruit those with the best expertise for the various tasks, and that the burden is distributed fairly

[2699] Personnel who make themselves available for offshore operations must be taken care of

[2700] The Armed Forces' ability to take responsibility for personnel upon their return home, and to ensure that individuals receive health care and other follow-up when needed, must be further strengthened

[2701] Although the civilian health service will still have the primary responsibility for providing these services, the Armed Forces, through closer contact with the general public, will be able to identify and support those who need special assistance

[2702] The Armed Forces shall thus fulfill the role of point of contact between the individual and the civilian healthcare system

[2703] In addition, the Armed Forces should be able to provide support to personnel who experience mental health problems related to such service

[2704] The Armed Forces' medical service shall improve the quality of services within selection, monitoring of personnel in operations and aftercare

[2705] It should be emphasized that those who experience health problems as a result of injuries or illnesses during or after such service should be ensured satisfactory treatment as quickly as practicable

[2706] A system in which the Armed Forces purchases services from the civilian health service when needed, including internationally, will be considered

[2719] The career path of the commander and officers

[2720] New tasks and competence requirements require a strengthening of education in the Armed Forces

[2721] The education scheme is therefore proposed to be amended to achieve the goal of the right type of competence in the right place in the organization, and to contribute to costefficiency

[2722] The government has placed great emphasis on the Chief of Defence's recommendations in this regard

[2723] It is proposed that the education system in the Armed Forces be changed towards a system that is more compatible with and flexible in relation to the civilian education system, which to a greater extent reduces absences from and interruptions in active service due to education, and which contributes to meeting the Armed Forces' future competence needs

[2724] An overarching principle is that the right type of education is provided at the right time in the career and is adapted to the demands of the service

[2725] This also reflects that parts of the commanding corps are increasingly specializing

[2726] Harmonization with the civilian degree system will make it easier for the Armed Forces to use the civilian education system in cases where this is appropriate

[2727] Such harmonization will not affect the Armed Forces' freedom to define the content of the education itself

[2728] The quality requirements for bachelor's and master's education shall be the same as in the civilian university and college system

[2729] The Armed Forces' education system shall build up and possess competence focused on subject areas that are directly related to the Armed Forces' primary activities

[2730] planning, management and support of military operations, as well as the operation and development of the military organization

[2731] Within these areas, the Armed Forces' schools shall be high-quality institutions

[2732] Education must emphasize the development of the ability to conceptual and critical thinking, as well as creativity – qualities that are crucial for the Armed Forces to be further developed in line with the ambition of transformation and a more adaptable Defence Force

[2733] The education system must satisfy military needs, and cover areas where there is no equivalent civilian provision or educational offer in NATO or among our allies

[2734] The Armed Forces will rely to a greater extent than previously on purchasing educational packages from the civilian university and college system, or abroad, where such may be appropriate and cost-effective

[2735] In addition to the military academy and staff academy, shorter branch-specific courses will supplement the education

[2736] The Armed Forces will increasingly use "on the job training" to meet the need for practical, position-specific competence

[2737] A more detailed description of the division of responsibilities in the education system is given in chapter

[2738] The new education scheme increases flexibility, gives the Armed Forces a broader recruitment base and helps to solve future competence needs and challenges

[2739] After completing officer training school and following compulsory service, one can choose either military school education, technical education or appointment as a department commander

[2740] Alternatively, one can choose to take a civilian education outside the Armed Forces, and then return to the Armed Forces and obtain a position, provided that the Armed Forces have a need for the relevant type of competence

[2741] Basic officer training

[2742] The command school The basic command education is the basic level of education for the command corps

[2743] This education should provide competence and experience to fill management positions or specialist positions at lower levels in the organization

[2744] The existing one year officer training schools with subsequent compulsory service will be modernized, and a more flexible and practically oriented education course over two years will be introduced

[2745] Education shall be achieved to a greater extent through St.prop

[2746] no. 42 The further modernization of the Armed Forces in the period 2005–2008 service at a department and a separate commander's course

[2747] The modernized command schools will focus on leadership development and basic military and specialized skills based on the needs of the defense branches

[2748] The content of today's command schools also includes basic soldier skills, which largely coincides with the content of initial service

[2749] By implementing education to a greater extent in conjunction with other educational activities, and in the operational environments that have the best conditions for doing this, the foundation is laid for more targeted and effective education under realistic conditions

[2750] This will increase the overall quality

[2751] Recruitment for officer training will take place in two ways

[2752] Either by recruiting personnel directly from high school as is the case today, or by recruiting personnel from departments under initial service

[2753] A flexible education and recruitment model is being planned, where specific needs are the guiding principle for implementation

[2754] It is also important that the scheme ensures good recruitment of women, which requires the possibility of direct admission to officer training from high school, since women are not subject to military service

[2755] Such a flexible arrangement could lead to relatively different implementation models between the branches of defense, based on the needs of the branches of defense, and also within the branches of defense, even though the results and formal requirements will be the same

[2757] Military school and bachelor's degree

[2758] It is proposed to introduce a three-year war school in all branches of defense

[2760] Education is made flexible, so that both shorter education courses and combinations with civilian education are possible, where this is appropriate based on the needs of the Armed Forces

[2761] Eligible applicants are, as a general rule, those who have completed basic officer training

[2762] Exceptions to this may be made, based on the needs of the Armed Forces

[2765] The content of the education shall be designed with the aim of primarily covering the need for specialized expertise at a lower level

[2766] This means that the service that follows immediately after military school cannot alone be decisive for the education

[2767] The Military Academy will continue to play an important role in influencing personal development, leadership skills, attitudes and professional codes throughout the officer corps

[2773] The personnel will thereby avoid interruptions in service, and the number of relocations as a result of education will be reduced

[2784] Education at master's level shall be research-based and in line with the general requirements for master's education

[2785] Corresponding staff training abroad is an important supplement and is equated with national staff training

[2786] Civilian master's education, or parts of such education, can be distilled with national staff education, based on the needs of the Armed Forces and upon application

[2797] Civilian personnel

[2798] The Armed Forces recruit civilian personnel who initially have the necessary formal competence to perform their duties

[2799] However, personnel will need to further develop their skills during their professional careers in the Norwegian Defence Forces

[2800] This will happen both through experience and through various forms of further and continuing education

[2801] Responsibility for continuing and further education for civilians, and leave arrangements in connection with this, shall lie with the Armed Forces Training Center and the local commanders

[2802] Research and competence centers

[2803] The Armed Forces' educational institutions shall primarily focus on areas that are directly relevant to the Armed Forces' core activities

[2804] Considering

[2805] available resources, including personnel, which will be a critical factor, there is a need for increased concentration of educational activities to establish effective units in certain areas

[2806] The Armed Forces must critically assess how educational activities can be made more efficient

[2807] In cases where civilian offerings exist that meet the Armed Forces' needs equally effectively, the Armed Forces shall purchase training packages from them

[2808] In this context, it should also be considered to purchase educational places abroad, preferably with close allies, rather than building up national expertise in narrow fields

[2809] The Armed Forces' research, development and education activities shall strengthen cooperation with civilian professional communities where this is appropriate

[2810] In this context, it is important that the purchase of civil services is quality assured, based on a comprehensive system

[2811] Both the number of educational institutions and the number of man-years must in the future be assessed and adjusted in relation to what is cost-effective and quality-assured

[2812] Educational activities must also be made the subject of comprehensive prioritization, especially in light of the need to prioritize operational activities

[2813] At the same time, the Armed Forces must maintain a high level of expertise within the specifically defined professional military areas

[2814] The changed portfolio of tasks and the reduced number of students at the Armed Forces' educational institutions overall means a reduction in the budget allocated to them

[2815] Further steps in this direction – also beyond those described in this proposition – will be considered during the period

[2816] Transformation places increased demands on education, research and development in areas of a conceptual nature related to military organization and the use of military power

[2817] The Armed Forces' expertise environments must therefore be designed so that they can meet these requirements and support transformation, while primarily supporting education

[2818] This also includes the need for exchange of information and close cooperation with similar institutions among our allies

[2819] Research and development

[2820] R&D) is crucial to further developing and streamlining the Armed Forces' operational organization, and to achieving transformation of the military forces

[2821] This applies to all input factors that are relevant to solving the Armed Forces' tasks

[2822] The main challenge is to identify in which areas the Armed Forces should have their own R&D capacity, in which areas the Armed Forces should cooperate with our allies, and in which areas it is appropriate for the Armed Forces to use R&D that is produced externally

[2823] Both cost-effectiveness and assessments related to critical competence are factors that will influence the answer to this

[2824] The last factor applies not only specifically to the individual subject areas, but also generally to the 2003–2004 St.prp

[2825] The further modernization of the Armed Forces in the period 2005–2008 will maintain the necessary expertise in connection with the procurement of goods and services for the Armed Forces

[2826] Within the overall framework of R&D, there will be opportunities for increased cost-efficiency, especially within development activities

[2827] Development of materiel for own use must be limited to the Armed Forces' needs in areas where other alternatives are not available or cost-effective

[2828] An increased focus on this could open the way for a reduction in R&D spending. R&D financed through the defense budget currently amounts to approximately NOK 1.2 billion annually

[2829] In terms of size, this amount is mainly distributed as just over a third to FFI, and half to major development projects and development within major or minor procurement projects

[2830] The rest goes to financing smaller projects in industry and at other research institutions, including colleges and universities

[2831] Based on the above, as well as the Armed Forces' generally pressured financial situation, a critical assessment of the total framework has been carried out with a special focus on development activities, and a reduction in R&D expenditure is recommended, cf. chapter

[2832] The total R&D activity in the Armed Forces is very limited by international standards

[2833] To create the best possible environment for successful and cost-effective R&D, it would be appropriate to pool the efforts of the business

[2834] However, it is important to point out that integration or co-location of all R&D activities in the Armed Forces is not a goal in itself

[2835] The most important factor will in any case be that the R&D environments in the Armed Forces pull in the same direction and collaborate across disciplines

[2836] Through the establishment of integrated management, the Ministry of Defence has strengthened its capacity for managing R&D in the Armed Forces

[2837] The most important factor for management will be the identification of the Armed Forces' needs

[2838] In governance, it is therefore important to facilitate a dialogue between the R&D communities and the Armed Forces in general

[2839] The R&D that is carried out must be of a high standard, while Norway must base itself on an R&D strategy in which the potential of international cooperation is fully exploited

[2849] The FSS shall be developed into a nationally and internationally recognized institution for contemporary expertise in the following fields: military power – including military history and military thought, international law of war, security and defense policy, as well as joint operations and comprehensive military leadership

[2850] A review of the activities at FSS will be carried out with strict prioritization of work areas

[2853] At the same time, it is necessary to have a gradual approach to the development of the FSS

[2866] The military schools The military schools will continue with their current location

[2867] The military academies shall meet the needs of the various branches of defense for professional competence, and lay the foundation for service in the defense in leadership and staff positions

[2868] The military academies shall be the educational powerhouse of the defense branches, and education must be based on close collaboration with the operational environments and with the educational and expertise environments, both academically and in terms of resources

[2869] Education at the military academies must be based on close cooperation with, among others, the FSS

[2870] Military schools should also use the purchase of civilian education packages where this is appropriate

[2871] In light of the above, and as a result of fewer classes at the military academies and a reduced number of students, a significant reduction in operational and man years at the military academies shall be made – as soon as possible and no later than the end of 2007 – in order to contribute to the general goal of freeing up resources for operational activities in the branches of defense and material investments

[2872] High competence in management and logistics is a prerequisite for the Armed Forces' activities to be efficient and rational

[2873] In the future, the activities of the Armed Forces will be centered to a greater extent on operations, both nationally and internationally, and to a significantly lesser extent on the management and maintenance of a relatively large war structure and base organization

[2874] The Armed Forces' expertise needs are therefore shifting from primarily peacekeeping management and operations, towards supporting operations

[2875] Management education must therefore be changed and adapted to these changing competence needs

[2876] Today, the Armed Forces itself conducts both shorter and longer-term training in general management disciplines

[2877] Parts of this education are purchased as courses, and parts are carried out by our own expertise groups

[2878] What this education has in common is that it takes place under the auspices of the Armed Forces' educational institutions, mainly the military academies and the Armed Forces Management School (FFS

[2879] In the future, the Armed Forces will seek to make greater use of civilian educational opportunities or military schools abroad in this area

[2880] This generally applies within subject areas that are not unique to the Armed Forces, and where relevant expertise environments are available externally

[2881] At the same time, it is desirable that the Armed Forces' own expertise environments increasingly direct their activities towards core military expertise, with a strong emphasis on logistical support for operations

[2882] This results in a reduced need for the type of education offered at the current Defence Administration School

[2883] The shift will also result in changes at the military academy level

[2884] Technical education

[2885] Technical expertise is an important foundation for the Armed Forces' activities

[2886] The Armed Forces depend on technical user and maintenance expertise to ensure that the systems used are available and perform optimally

[2887] Technical expertise and systems understanding are important in order to utilize technology effectively in operations, and to be able to implement systems that support operational concepts in an optimal manner

[2888] In this situation, it is important that the Armed Forces find appropriate ways to meet this need for expertise

[2889] This will include utilizing civilian expertise environments and educational offerings where available, and focusing our own resources on needs that are not covered by civilian educational offerings

[2890] The Armed Forces currently have a number of educational offerings, which in several areas can be equated with civilian educational offerings, but with a military-oriented focus or specialization

[2891] As a result of the changes in the command system, and also the very structure of the Armed Forces, the educational needs within these fields will change

[2892] In many cases, educational volumes will be reduced, while demands for specialization will increase

[2893] In the future, the Armed Forces will seek to utilize other and more cost-effective ways of organizing this education, through better cooperation internally within the Armed Forces, by outsourcing entire elements of this education to civilian educational institutions, or through collaborative solutions to offer militarily relevant specializations at civilian educational institutions

[2894] Especially within technical education – engineering/bachelor – there will be an effort in the future to utilize the flexibility and opportunities inherent in such organizational forms to a greater extent

[2986] The further adaptation of the Armed Forces' force production and logistics and support activities2 7.1 Overall principles and objectives for the further adaptation of the Armed Forces' force production and logistics and support activities

[2987] It is of fundamental importance for future operational capability that the Armed Forces are run in a cost-effective manner

[2988] One objective of this long-term plan is therefore to outline improvements in the form of a set of clear goals and concrete measures within strengthening production and logistics and support activities

[2989] The resources that are released will help ensure the transformation and modernization of the Armed Forces' operational forces

[2990] The business shall primarily serve the operational needs of the Armed Forces

[2991] Therefore, the operational structure, as described in previous chapters, forms the basis for how the logistics and support structure should be further developed

[2992] Overall, the recommended measures will shift resource use by approximately NOK 2 billion per year away from logistics and support activities to operational activities, including international operations and material investments

[2993] This is a crucial contribution to ensuring a balanced structure

[2994] The following groups of measures are recommended

[2995] – Increased availability and relevance in support of operational activities

[2996] The usability of logistics and support activities will be significantly increased

[2997] This will increase the relevance and quality of the support provided

[2998] The term "logistics and support activities" is appropriate to describe the part of the Armed Forces that is affected in this chapter

[2999] The term helps to focus on the fact that this activity encompasses all activities in the Armed Forces that support the operational structure

[3000] The business includes organizational levels and activities within FMO and the defense sector in general that deliver services and products that contribute to the operational business achieving its goals

[3001] The logistics and support business shall primarily obtain its assignments and funds through horizontal trade with operational businesses, in a structured customer-supplier relationship

[3002] Logistics and support activities are – in addition to all logistics that do not directly support operations – property management, research and development (R&D) as well as administrative and management services

[3003] More efficient organization of force production

[3004] More efficient models for strength production are being used

[3005] Two considerations in particular are emphasized

[3006] First and foremost, a development towards integrating larger parts of today's education and competence centers into the force production departments

[3007] This is an essential prerequisite for creating the necessary personnel space to realize the operational ambition

[3008] – Furthermore, it is necessary to extract additional competence and economic benefits by establishing new, cross-branch force production activities, for example through the proposal to establish the Norwegian Defence Force's competence centre for logistics at Sessvollmoen and a joint competence centre for command, control and information systems (KKIS) at Jørstadmoen (Lillehammer

[3011] The basic principle for the ongoing restructuring is that holistic thinking – regardless of branch affiliation – should characterize the activities of the Ministry to a greater extent

[3012] Synergy effects are also achieved by co-locating related businesses to one common area

[3013] In this way, economies of scale can be exploited, for example by establishing joint management and supply services, joint education and competence centers, etc

[3014] Activities in the Armed Forces must, where relevant, be comparable with similar activities in the private sector, so that both quality and profitability can be measured and assessed

[3015] The goal is to create a more rational operation

[3016] At the same time, the 2003–2004 St.prop

[3041] The assumptions for the financial calculations of individual measures

[3042] Method and assumptions for the holistic economic

[3043] The economic consequences of the government's recommendations are presented in chapter

[3044] Here, only the methodology used to compare the alternatives is outlined

[3045] All assessments of organizational changes are made from a total economic perspective, which in addition to NOK also includes quality, flexibility and availability

[3046] The profitability of the various alternatives considered has been calculated using the present value model

[3047] This is so that all the expenses associated with the alternatives, both in terms of operations and investments in EBA, can be taken into account in a realistic manner

[3048] The present value model provides a basis for comparing alternative solutions with different future cash flows, by showing how these future cash flows are valued today

[3049] Future cash flows are discounted using a required rate of return

[3050] A 4% real return requirement has been used in the profitability calculations, based on the fact that internal reorganizations are considered to have low risk, and a 20-year time horizon

[3051] Only measures that are profitable in the shorter term (preferably within a 4-year perspective) are prioritized

[3052] The price development for the Defence's operating costs is expected to follow inflation, with the exception of salary-related costs, where 2% real wage growth per year is assumed

[3053] Cash flows mainly include receipts and payments for personnel and infrastructure

[3054] Personnel-related costs are categorized into the Armed Forces' various personnel categories

[3055] Infrastructure expenses are divided into investments, sales and disposal, upgrades and operating costs

[3056] In cases where alternatives are assumed to result in significant differences in material costs or other operating costs, this is calculated separately

[3057] Otherwise, material-related costs for the total structure are captured in the total calculations, cf. chapter

[3058] The calculations have been followed up by sensitivity analyses, which have studied the impact that changes in the various cost elements have on the profitability assessment

[3059] Furthermore, it is considered where

[3060] how profitability is affected by changes in return requirements and time horizon

[3061] The results from the calculations are further assessed and prioritized with regard to a short-term opportunity to realize necessary investments within the current defense budgets

[3062] In options with margin

[3063] For differences in present value, where the sensitivity analyses show that the mutual profitability of the alternatives is uncertain, rapid realization of the savings, as well as nonquantifiable factors, is given greater weight

[3064] All alternatives are subject to a comprehensive assessment

[3065] In two areas, an overall potential for man-year reductions and operational savings has been estimated, without this being further specified

[3066] In order to realize the operational structure recommended by this proposal, it is crucial to include these man-years

[3067] This applies to management, command structure and foreign positions on the one hand, and the education, skills and school sector on the other

[3068] In these sectors, a total reduction of 750 net man years is assumed, of which at least 200 net foreign positions, or measures that provide equivalent savings

[3069] The precise distribution of these cuts/savings will be clarified through the Ministry's follow-up of the Storting's consideration of this proposal

[3092] Proposal for the closure of activities at the Regional Command Southern Norway

[3093] As part of the restructuring of the command structure and the top strategic leadership, it is proposed to discontinue the activities of the Regional Command Southern Norway (LDKS) in Trondheim

[3094] This move is appropriate for three reasons

[3095] Firstly, it is necessary to carry out a further rationalisation of the command structure, with the aim of transferring resources and responsibilities to the operational units

[3096] Secondly, developments in information and communication technology mean that each individual link in the chain of command can handle a wider span of control

[3097] This enables a more streamlined command structure

[3098] Thirdly, the transition from a mobilization defense to a reaction defense has meant that the need for Regional Commands has been reduced, and that tasks can be partly transferred to the Joint Operational Headquarters (FOHK) and partly to the HV districts

[3099] The latter is possible because quality reforms in HQ mean that each individual HQ district will be able to take control of the territorial tasks themselves to a greater extent

[3100] Tasks related to the advanced warehouses in Trøndelag are handled by FOHK, in collaboration with the new merged HV district in North and South Trøndelag, with district management in Værnes

[3101] This involves a concentration of the Armed Forces' activities in Trøndelag to Værnes, with HV education and the management of the new HV district

[3114] Changes in the Army

[3115] Main features of the new organization

[3116] The army is proposed to be reorganized

[3117] The purpose of the organization is to strengthen operational capability

[3118] There are several fundamental changes compared to today's organization

[3119] The Army's operational force production and competence activities will be organized into two parts, the Army Forces (HSTY) and the Army Transformation and Doctrine Command (TRADOK

[3120] Education and training of the Army's operational capabilities will take place in the operational departments

[3123] In addition, an organization is being established that will be able to develop and adapt the Army, based on the prevailing military professional guidelines or changing political conditions at any given time

[3124] The main task will be, within the strategies and frameworks set by strategic management, to oversee the development, adaptation and implementation of new concepts for the Army within doctrine, structural elements, operational capacities and materiel

[3125] This organization is continued and developed in TRADOC

[3131] This organizational change also enables the Army to increase the proportion of deployable forces with short reaction times

[3680] FLO/Heavy Maintenance Division

[3681] The aim is for FLO/HM to be reorganized as soon as possible and no later than the end of the period into a state/privately owned limited company, and separated from the Armed Forces organization

[3682] It is a prerequisite that such a company should be able to compete on equal terms with private suppliers for the services the Armed Forces demand in this area, and that it should at the same time be able to deliver services in the private market

[3683] There are no key reasons for the state to be a long-term owner in such a workshop business when it is put out to competition

[3684] If it is not appropriate to establish the company as privately owned in the first instance, it should – after it has been properly established – be transferred to the Ministry of Trade and Industry, and managed from there based on ordinary return requirements until the company can be privatized

[3685] In preparation for this, the Ministry will continue to work on deepening and specifying the basis for operating FLO/TV on a commercial basis, and on the financial consequences of a separation, including the need for capital injections

[3686] The Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Trade and Industry will be actively involved in this process

[3687] The activities within FLO/TV largely revolve around heavy/industrial maintenance of vehicles, aircraft and naval vessels

[3688] This is a type of activity that the Armed Forces do not have to carry out themselves, but which can be purchased from national and/or international players

[3689] Furthermore, a separation would give FLO/TV the opportunity to compete for assignments in the rest of the market, both nationally and internationally

[3690] The change in the form of affiliation is primarily justified by the objective of creating better alignment between actual maintenance needs and existing production capacity in the Armed Forces, thereby creating greater flexibility in the event of fluctuations in the market and in the assignment portfolio

[3691] Furthermore, such a change in the form of affiliation will lead to a stronger focus on efficiency, including by establishing a clear distinction between the Armed Forces as a customer and FLO/TV as a supplier of goods and services

[3692] This will create better conditions for real horizontal trade and will also allow FLO/TV to compete for assignments on the open market

[3693] The reorganization will mean that man-years captured in FLO/TV at the time of release, comprising a maximum of 1,250 man-years at the time of establishment, will be taken out of FMO, cf

[3858] The further modernization of the Armed Forces in the period 2005–

[3859] Implementation of the further restructuring

[3860] The entirety of the measures described in this proposition involves a restructuring of the Norwegian Defence Forces towards increased relevance and operability, as well as more efficient task execution within logistics and support activities

[3861] The measures enable – where they are implemented in an efficient and timely manner – a further transformation towards a more modern and flexible Defence

[3862] The transformation must be based on the following principles

[3863] – Continuous restructuring

[3864] The Armed Forces must continuously adapt to changes in the security policy landscape and further develop the organization towards more resource-efficient services

[3865] This means that additional measures will be identified during the period to achieve the overall objectives of the restructuring

[3866] – Strategic management and clear responsibilities

[3867] The main responsibility for implementing the transformation lies with the Chief of Defence as head of the Defence's military organisation, and in this capacity he is responsible for achieving the overall transformation objectives (cf. Chapter 8.2 below

[3868] These will be broken down so that the individual manager will be given independent responsibility for the results of the transformation. – Power and pace

[3869] The measures must be implemented quickly and with force immediately

[3870] planning has been completed

[3871] This is particularly important as the realization of operational ambition requires a significant release of resources within logistics and support activities. – Transparency and communication

[3872] It is a prerequisite for success that the Armed Forces' employees, and others who will be greatly affected by the further transformation, are kept informed in a timely and appropriate manner, and are included in a dialogue about the challenges and opportunities the process presents

[3873] Overall objectives

[3874] The most important goal for the restructuring 2005–2008 is for the Armed Forces to be as well-equipped as possible to handle future challenges and to be able to appear as the most effective security policy instrument possible

[3875] This requires a modernization of the operational structure as outlined in Chapter 5, implementation of the personnel policy measures outlined in Chapter 6, and a transfer of resources from logistics and support activities to operational operations and investments, cf. Chapter

[3876] The following restructuring goals are therefore recommended, based on the measures outlined in this proposal

[3877] At full effect, a minimum of NOK 2 billion (2004) will be shifted from logistics and support activities to operational activities and material investments, relative to the 2004 level

[3878] Of this, a net minimum of NOK 600 million will be released from the Armed Forces Logistics Organization

[3879] At the same time, the following financial and administrative objectives are sought to be achieved

[3880] An estimated 34 billion 2004-kr in total is allocated to material investments during the period; the number of man-years in the Armed Forces' military organization is reduced to an estimated 15,000, excluding gains related to the further modernization of FLO (cf. chapter 8.5.6); the Armed Forces' properties, buildings and facilities are reduced to a maximum of 3.5 million sq m (the goal of the ongoing restructuring is a reduction from 6 million to 4 million sq m); and rental costs per sq m are reduced by up to 20%

[3881] The goals must be achieved as soon as possible and at the latest by the end of the year

[3882] As outlined in Chapter 1, the overall objectives for the period up to and including 2005 remain fixed

[3883] This goal applies to the fact that the Norwegian Armed Forces' military organization will consist of a maximum of 15,300 man-years by the end of

[3903] Control of operating cost developments An absolute prerequisite for realizing this development is that the underlying factors that drive the Armed Forces' cost developments are addressed

[3904] Subsequent calculations show that the Armed Forces' operating expenses in particular have increased more than inflation over the years, while material investment costs are increasing as a result of an increasingly higher technological level

[3905] In terms of operating costs, it is imperative to achieve future development that is in line with developments in society as a whole

[3906] The cost calculations that form the basis for the recommendation on financial frameworks are therefore based on rates of operating cost growth that are significantly lower than historical rates

[3907] The challenges that cost developments entail, both in terms of operations and material investments, are being addressed through overall goals related to the Armed Forces' operating costs and a number of specific measures

[3908] These include, among others

[3909] – Strengthened management of the allocation of operating funds, with priority given to operational activities over support activities – Proposals and measures related to personnel with the aim of having the same salary development as society at large (commander system, education, revision of the Armed Forces' salary system, etc

[3910] – Multinational cooperation and stricter prioritization of projects to achieve better utilization of the resources used for equipment investments and operation of the equipment

[3927] Key instruments in the restructuring

[3928] Although the 2002–2005 restructuring has been largely successful, a need for additional instruments related to the management of the restructuring has become clear

[3929] This applies especially to the personnel council

[3930] The most important instruments for the period 2005–2008 are outlined below

[3931] Strategic goals and performance management

[3932] The Ministry of Defence is continuously working on further developing comprehensive and coherent management of processes from the planning stage to follow-up of results

[3933] The Ministry's management concept is based on strategic goal and performance management of subordinate agencies, where the formulation of goals and performance requirements/performance indicators is central

[3934] The Norwegian Defence Military Organisation (FMO) and the other agencies will be monitored in agency management by the Ministry through the objectives outlined above, specified through performance requirements, as well as through follow-up in relation to a set of defined performance indicators and identified risk factors

[3935] An important contribution to this will be that FMO and the other agencies use common integrated management systems (IFS) to the greatest extent possible

[3936] As part of the management concept, proactive risk management (proactive risk) and balanced scorecard management (balanced scorecard) are included

[3937] PR should be used at every level of management, and is intended to ensure goal achievement by identifying and managing the most critical risk factors in relation to selected goals

[3938] The Ministry of Defence, for its part, focuses on the implementation of the adopted strategy for the defence sector, expressed through a strategic vision

[3939] Each goal should be formulated so that the purpose of the goal itself and the end state upon goal achievement are clearly stated

[3940] In line with principles of good goal and results management, the goal statement thus specifies what is to be achieved or delivered, without unnecessarily specifying how this is to be done

[3941] Managers at every level of management are expected to plan, prioritize and implement their own activities within given frameworks, so that the set goals are achieved

[3942] The Chief of Defence is responsible for overall goal achievement in FMO, and must report deviations and expected goal achievement throughout the operational year to the Ministry of Defence

[3943] The Chief of Defence and the other heads of departments, and each individual commander under them in the Armed Forces, are responsible for reaping the benefits of the restructuring and identifying tasks that will no longer be performed in light of new priorities

[3944] This is particularly important in view of the formidable task of reducing the actual growth in operating costs that the Armed Forces have experienced in recent years, so that it is in line with the assumptions that the Chief of Defence has based on his military expert report (MFU

[3945] Agencies are expected to manage risk within their own operations by identifying and following up on risk

[3946] Proactive risk management together with balanced performance management will improve the ability to achieve the set goals for the defense sector, and further improvement in goal achievement is expected in the coming years

[3947] Personnel policy instruments

[3948] The recommendations outlined in Chapter 6 are critical to the transition

[3949] Here, the new command structure and measures related to it are crucial, by

[3950] – introduce a duty to order all commanders, officers and certain categories of civilians to international 2003–2004 St.prop

[3952] These measures will provide a relatively rapid improvement in operational capability, and in the long term will also largely ensure that the personnel profile can be more easily adapted to the needs of the Defence

[3953] However, the Armed Forces also have a significant and more short-term need to downsize the organization

[3954] This will be resolved in 2005–2008 primarily through: new set-up plans that must be continuously updated; establishment of a support organization for, and early identification of, redundant employees; and continuation of previous and new various retirement incentive measures (AST

[3955] Restructuring and downsizing should take place in parallel

[3956] As there is a mismatch between the requirements for new positions in operational activities and the personnel expected

[3957] released in the logistics and support business, a significant transformation challenge is expected on the personnel side

[3958] It will therefore be necessary to consciously manage in accordance with the Armed Forces' real competence needs when designing and implementing the downsizing process. New deployment plans will be drawn up in parallel with the Storting's consideration of this proposition

[3960] Personnel who are not reassigned when the new staffing plan is completed will become redundant
