[3985] The further modernization of the Armed Forces in the period 2005–

[3986] Introduction of modern information and communication technology (ICT) Expanded and adapted use of technology will be an important tool in the further restructuring of the Armed Forces

[3987] New solutions, especially within information and communication technology, create significant potential for further efficiency improvements, both within operational activities, and particularly within logistics and support activities

[3988] Here, increased use of standardized solutions, combined with limitations in the type and number of existing solutions and better coordination of these, could yield major gains

[3989] This is both in terms of cost-effectiveness and with a view to being able to utilize information in a better way, also as a basis for operational activities

[3990] To get the full effect of new information and communication technology, it is also necessary to simultaneously change the processes, organizational patterns and structures that surround it

[3991] The development towards network-based defence, cf. box 5.4, is an example of this

[3992] This also has important cost aspects

[3993] Modern technology can be expensive in isolation, and also contribute to increasing operating costs in some parts of the Armed Forces' ICT activities

[3994] By consciously using the introduction of new information and communication technology as an integrated part of a broader restructuring, an overall reduction in total operating costs will still be achieved through profit extraction in other parts of the organization

[3995] As part of the ongoing restructuring, the following principles will be used as a basis for the further development of the Armed Forces' information infrastructure: – The coherence and structure of the use of technology, as well as the standards used, must contribute to the Armed Forces being able to operate effectively together with current and new partners, both nationally and internationally; – emphasis must be placed on establishing services that are organized in such a way that they enable rapid and flexible support for new and changed activities, and in line with changes made by allies where system cooperation exists; and – a development must be sought in which the type and number of information and communication solutions are reduced and better coordinated, both within and across different grading levels

[3996] This will also make an important contribution to interoperability

[4157] Premises for the development of the Armed Forces

[4158] The restructuring will help the Armed Forces to be better equipped to meet future challenges

[4159] The benefits of the restructuring are therefore not only achieved in the current and next long-term period

[4160] The steps being taken now also help lay the foundation for better Norwegian defense in the period

[4161] Below is a brief outline of some of the challenges facing the Norwegian Defence Force, how the steps being taken in the ongoing restructuring contribute to strengthening the Norwegian Defence Force's ability to meet these, and what challenges remain

[4162] Unpredictability requires a continuously flexible defense

[4163] Norwegian security has been radically improved in relation to classic security threats, but new security challenges have emerged

[4164] The nature and extent of these depend on a number of different and complex factors, and are difficult to predict with great accuracy

[4165] This is accentuated by the strategic development trends that have been described in more detail earlier, where the risk picture is characterized by unpredictability and new threats, international cooperation patterns are changing dynamically, and technological development is proceeding very rapidly

[4166] A flexible defense – which can meet a wide range of possible security challenges, which is adaptable and can continuously adapt to changes in the environment –

[4167] will be the best guarantee that Norway can meet the challenges that may arise

[4168] This requires the ability to think long-term and to discover and analyze new developments at an early stage, structures and organizational forms that are adaptable, as well as a high level of competence and willingness to change among personnel

[4169] The ongoing restructuring is contributing greatly to developing the Armed Forces in this direction, not least through the focus placed on the need for transformation, where a central objective is precisely to be at the forefront of developments in the time perspective over which one has a reasonable overview

[4170] In order to be able to handle unpredictability and adapt to constant changes in the environment, the Norwegian Defence Forces' forces and management and command structure must be designed to provide the fundamentals for a network-based organisation with intention-driven, self-organised units

[4171] Such an organization must allow decentralized management and problem solving through intention and framework management, so that a unified direction of development is achieved that still allows freedom of action, adaptability and flexibility

[4172] Given the unpredictability inherent in the longer term, it cannot be taken for granted that it is possible to plan realistically for future structures

[4173] It should therefore be sought to develop organically adaptable structures

[4174] Continued high support for the Armed Forces is crucial. Support for the Armed Forces in Norway is high

[4175] This is of great importance both for the Armed Forces' anchoring in the population, for the Armed Forces' ability to recruit qualified personnel and for the Armed Forces' financial basis

[4176] A continued high level of support for the Armed Forces will be crucial for the future of the Armed Forces

[4177] However, developments both within and outside the Armed Forces make this more demanding

[4178] While the Armed Forces have increased their response capability, they have become smaller in terms of volume, and are located and conduct their activities in fewer places in the country than previously, because their activities are concentrated within each region

[4179] The significant changes in the Armed Forces have also meant that fewer people are completing their first-time service

[4180] All of these are necessary consequences of developments, with a greatly changed risk picture, changed technology and the need to create a more operational and qualitatively improved defense in order to safeguard Norway's security in a new era

[4181] At the same time, the contact surfaces and points of contact between the Armed Forces and society could be reduced

[4182] Furthermore, profound changes in the risk picture and in Norway's security policy environment have meant that the comprehensive and clearly defined threat to Norwegian security that previously existed has disappeared

[4183] This has been replaced by a risk picture that is unpredictable and complex

[4184] The challenges to Norwegian security are not as clear in the St.prop

[4185] No. 42 2003–

[4186] The further modernization of the Armed Forces in the period 2005–2008, as before, is much more strongly linked to conditions and developments that have their origins and are played out far outside Norway and Norwegian territories

[4187] This makes the causal chains from these phenomena to Norwegian security complicated, which makes it more difficult to communicate the connections, and thus the rationale and function of the Armed Forces

[4188] However, the above challenges cannot be met by reintroducing yesterday's defenses and turning a blind eye to developments in Norway's wider surroundings

[4189] Something like this would be irresponsible from a security policy perspective as well as from an organizational and economic perspective

[4190] In the future, great emphasis must therefore be placed on measures that help ensure that the Armed Forces continue to appear as a visible and credible tool for securing Norway and Norwegian society's security interests, and that help to underpin a perception that the Armed Forces continue to fulfill a function that is at least as central and necessary as before

[4191] This requires active outreach activities on the part of the Norwegian Defence Forces

[4192] The most important prerequisite, however, will be to ensure that the Armed Forces remain relevant and capable of handling all of their tasks in an effective and credible manner, not least the national tasks in Norway and its surrounding areas

[4193] A main goal of the ongoing restructuring is precisely to contribute to this, by developing a high-quality defense that is deployable, responsive and mobile, and which is thus available to Norwegian authorities by being able to be deployed where and when the need arises

[4194] It is not least in order to be able to handle the challenges of the future nationally that the Armed Forces must be transformed

[4195] This will be a continuous and demanding process

[4196] Operational capability must be the core of the Armed Forces' activities. In the long term, too, the Armed Forces' ability to handle challenges related to unpredictability and a broad range of tasks must be decisive for the development of the organization

[4197] Being able to respond quickly to crises with appropriate operational solutions will be a success criterion

[4198] This is reinforced by the pace of change in terms of technological development

[4199] Within a realistic resource framework, strict priorities must therefore be set to ensure that investments in new equipment provide the desired flexibility and effect

[4200] The focus on multinational solutions will have to become much stronger in the future

[4201] All these conditions make great demands on organizational and mental flexibility

[4202] Although much has been achieved in the defense sector in Norway in recent years, defense transformation in Norway and in NATO has only just begun

[4203] Internationally, there is an increased focus on technological solutions and platforms that increase deployment capability, reduce logistics needs and optimize the benefits of modern information technology

[4204] Norway, as a small state with limited resources, must place decisive importance on the choices our close allies make regarding defense investments

[4205] Common and unified platforms across borders increase interoperability and cost-effectiveness by creating opportunities for a more common logistics and support structure

[4206] This could provide clear economies of scale

[4207] The major investments that will come after this planning period will have to be considered with this in mind

[4208] The development of network-based solutions will be continued

[4209] Existing solutions and organizations must therefore be assessed with a critical eye

[4210] In this area too, we only see the outlines of what future organizational solutions and opportunities will be, as well as the consequences this will have for operational activities

[4211] In a long-term perspective, it appears increasingly unlikely that the form of military organization we know today will be continued

[4212] Our defense must continue to emphasize continuous improvement of its operational capabilities, through close cooperation with our allies within the framework of new organizational solutions that utilize modern technology

[4213] Closer multinational cooperation, including through the North Sea Strategy, cf. box 3.4, will be crucial for Norway to create a forward-looking defense with increased operational capability

[4214] Likewise, the emphasis on quality in the operational structure is of critical importance

[4215] This is a key aspect of the ongoing transformation, and is further supported by the significant transfer of resources from logistics and support activities to operational activities recommended in this proposal

[4216] The Armed Forces must recruit the right personnel with the right expertise. In the current planning period (2002–2005), the Storting's order to reduce 5,000 man-years in the Defence Forces has meant that the focus has been on downsizing

[4217] This has been necessary due to reductions in the structure and changed tasks

[4218] However, both today and in the future, it is an equally central challenge for the Armed Forces to secure the right expertise through good recruitment

[4219] The Armed Forces must recruit the most suitable and most motivated, and ensure that 2003–2004 St.prop

[4220] No. 42 The further modernization of the Armed Forces in the period 2005–2008, the need for expertise at all levels, and within all service fields, is met

[4221] This applies particularly within the command and officer corps, but also on the civilian side

[4222] It is therefore important to prioritize and further develop recruitment strategies

[4223] The ever-increasing share of advanced technological defense equipment will make technological competence absolutely central

[4224] At the same time, the possibilities of technology must be anchored in dynamic concepts and doctrines, so that the effect is optimized

[4225] Seeing new opportunities at the intersection of technology, operational concept and organization will become increasingly important in the future

[4226] The armed forces must have personnel who combine increased specialization with an eye for the big picture

[4227] The ability and willingness to change must be institutionalized and rewarded

[4228] In the traditional Norwegian Armed Forces, the officer career has been characterized by a strong focus on broad competence through varied service

[4229] This has led to frequent replacements, and the service has largely been considered as training for the next level on the career ladder

[4230] Advanced technology will place great demands on specialized expertise and continuity

[4231] This will mean that personnel will stay in the various positions longer, and will specialize within more limited service areas

[4232] Horizontal careers could therefore become more common, which also has implications for the wage system

[4233] Within network-based operations, traditional dividing lines between branches of defense become more blurred

[4234] The goal is a flatter organization, which challenges traditional thinking about dividing the chain of command into strategic, operational and tactical levels

[4235] The need for international cooperation, multinational solutions and integrated structures will increase

[4236] This also sets competence requirements that must be met, which will have consequences for officer training and service patterns, where in the future increased emphasis must be placed on joint operational competence within a multinational framework

[4237] One of the main messages in this proposition is that quality must be prioritized over quantity

[4238] As a result of technological development, and the expectation from society that the Armed Forces will perform its tasks in an optimal manner, this must also characterize the Armed Forces' expertise environments

[4239] Smaller and more concentrated expertise environments with few employees can produce just as great an effect as staff-rich environments, provided that staff are recruited

[4240] nell with competence, motivation and interest in the relevant field

[4241] However, there will be a lower limit to what can be characterized as a research environment

[4242] To create synergy, such environments must be better connected to the rest of the Armed Forces organization

[4243] In the long term, recruitment, specialization, quality and continuity will be key words for the Armed Forces' personnel policy, and will be crucial for the Armed Forces' further development

[4244] This proposition lays the foundation for these considerations to be met in the future, through, among other things, a new command system and a new education system

[4245] The changes in the personnel area proposed in this proposal constitute the most important structural measures to achieve the goal of a more flexible defense that can be continuously adapted to developments in the framework conditions and the challenges in the security landscape, both in the short and longer term

[4246] The Armed Forces must gain control over the growth in expenditure and, through further rationalisation, create space to prioritise materiel investments. Through the measures outlined in this proposition, significant steps are being taken to gain control over the Armed Forces' expenditure and help to create space for greater materiel investments

[4247] Nevertheless, significant challenges will remain, related to factors over which the Defence Forces itself has no control

[4248] These will have to be met through further streamlining of operations, both during and after the period

[4249] The armed forces have traditionally, and especially in the last 20 years, experienced strong growth in their spending

[4250] The defence's operating expenses, primarily personnel costs, have increased significantly more than the cost trend in society at large

[4251] The recommendations above, regarding the establishment of a corps with department commanders, are important measures to gain control over this, in addition to ensuring an appropriate competence profile

[4252] The same is true of the recommendations that the Armed Forces' salary policy be reviewed and revised, with the aim of achieving greater control and predictability, and with the aim of ensuring that cost growth per manyear cannot exceed the corresponding growth in society at large

[4253] The proposals for overall and specific goals related to the Armed Forces' operating costs and man-year development for the next planning period are of central importance in this context

[4254] That Forsvaren succeeds in achieving these goals is crucial for its further development

[4255] In any case, it is a reality that there are aspects of the development of operating costs over which the Armed Forces itself has no control

[4256] In order to meet the assumptions regarding cost growth that form the basis for the cost calculations of the structure recommended above, the Armed Forces must therefore implement continuous rationalization measures – pursuant to the St.prop

[4257] No. 42 2003–

[4258] The further modernization of the Armed Forces in the period 2005–2008 exceeds those specified in this proposition

[4259] Only in this way can space be created to invest in the Defence's operational units, both in terms of operations and material investments

[4260] With regard to material investments in particular, however, there is a further challenge in addition to the growth in operating costs, namely that the expenses related to the Armed Forces' material investments are becoming increasingly higher per unit (so called technological depreciation

[4261] This is due to an increasingly higher technological level, which in most cases means that the price per unit increases significantly from one generation of equipment to the next

[4262] To some extent, this is a factor beyond our control, because it depends on the willingness of the major players to pay extra for extra performance

[4263] So far, there is little indication that this trend has slowed down

[4264] Some control over this development can nevertheless be achieved, partly through new ways of procuring, partly through a deeper and broader use of multinational cooperation and off-the-shelf solutions for procurement, and partly by reducing the number of “platforms” (vessels, aircraft, vehicles, etc.) as the performance of each platform improves

[4265] With regard to reducing the number of platforms, however, the room for manoeuvre within a national framework is limited, because in most areas we can identify a "critical mass" – that is, the minimum number the organisation must have in order to be able to produce and maintain sufficient expertise

[4266] A strategy for significant volume reductions will therefore largely have to be combined with a strategy in which we enter into broader multinational cooperation

[4267] This is, for example, very relevant with regard to the new generation of fighter aircraft

[4268] Given that the Storting agrees with and follows up on the recommendations of this proposition regarding structure and financing, the Armed Forces will have good opportunities to develop further in a positive direction during the restructuring period

[4269] In the longer term – in the period 2010–2020 – the Armed Forces are nevertheless facing very significant challenges, including those related to renewing large parts of the Army's and virtually all of the Air Force's equipment fleets

[4270] How big this challenge will be depends on the extent to which the Armed Forces succeed in controlling the growth in operating costs, as well as finding strategies to minimize the effects of technological increases in cost

[4271] Even with the most optimistic forecasts, however, it will not be possible to carry out all of these material procurements within the framework of a flat budget development

[4272] In this situation, the government and parliament will be faced with three possible choices: to finance parts of the investments through additional appropriations, to allow individual capabilities to be based on the structure in its entirety, or to allow the Armed Forces to enter into binding multinational cooperation that is both deeper and broader than that which is being implemented today

[4273] Box 9.1 elaborates on these options related to the fighter jet purchase

[4274] A lack of follow-up of the financing assumptions in this proposition will lead to these problems materializing more quickly and to a greater extent than is assumed here

[4275] The main point regarding the Armed Forces' future financial challenges is that the resource requirement within operational activities and materiel investments is so significant that there is no alternative to extracting maximum rationalization and efficiency gains within logistics and support activities

[4276] Although objections can always be raised against such cost-cutting measures, the alternative – reduced operational structure and thus reduced defense capability – is considerably worse

[4277] In the further development of the Armed Forces – both in the restructuring period 2005–2008 and thereafter – the most rational operation of the Armed Forces must therefore be a goal in itself

[4279] Financing of new fighter jets

[4280] After 2010, the F-16 aircraft will quickly reach the end of their operational life

[4281] The aircraft will then have been in use for more than 30 years

[4282] If Norway is to continue a national fighter aircraft capacity, the phasing in of a new aircraft type to replace the F-16 must therefore start over

[4283] Combat aircraft are absolutely crucial for the Armed Forces to be able to carry out their tasks in the future

[4284] The combat air force is one of the most flexible capabilities the Armed Forces have at their disposal, not least when it comes to asserting national sovereignty and crisis management

[4285] An effective combat aircraft capacity is a fundamental prerequisite for the Armed Forces to be able to function in line with established ambitions, without the risk of significant losses increasing drastically

[4286] The armed conflicts of the last decade have fully demonstrated how powerless a defense is if the opposing party can use the airspace for its own purposes without interference

[4308] Such a joint force will be able to collectively carry out many of the tasks that are included in the countries' prioritized activities

[4309] The tasks that will still have to be solved on a national basis will be able to be solved with aircraft that are not assigned to the joint force

[4331] A relevant defense – today and for the future

[4332] The recommendations put forward in this proposal will, if the Storting agrees with them, in themselves lay the foundation for a relevant Norwegian defense, with a significantly improved ability and flexibility to carry out its tasks

[4333] The restructuring will also entail a significantly increased focus on operational activities

[4334] All of this will in turn lead to increased public support and strengthen the Armed Forces' ability to recruit suitable personnel

[4335] Just as important as the specific measures recommended above, however, is the direction indicated for the development of the Armed Forces

[4336] Changes to the Armed Forces – whether called transformation, restructuring or modernization – will be the order of the day even after the restructuring period

[4337] It is the direction of these changes – prioritizing operational activities and material investments, maximizing the efficiency of logistics and support activities, increasing focus on creating a personnel structure with an appropriate competence, degree and age structure, and significantly increasing focus on multinational cooperation – that is the main message of this proposition

[4338] If these assumptions are violated, the Armed Forces will quickly move into new imbalances, resulting in a waste of resources and a reduced ability to solve tasks

[4339] However, if the Armed Forces are developed further, also after 2008, in line with these priorities, it will become a relevant and important security policy tool for the Norwegian authorities, also in the long term

[4401] Appendix 1: The Chief of Defence's principled view of the new Armed Forces, main challenges and long-term consequences

[4402] The expert military input to this proposition is based on the proposals in the Chief of Defence's Military Expert Report 2003 (MFU

[4403] The Chief of Defence's recommended force structure represents his professional military view of how the Defence Forces should be organised for the future within the framework of overall political frameworks and guidelines

[4404] The recommendation is thus a description of what would be the best possible use of the available funds

[4405] Resources must be directed towards what actually provides defensive capability, and the level of ambition must therefore be lowered in other areas

[4406] The Chief of Defence is satisfied that the current long-term proposal largely follows the expert military advice

[4407] The long-term proposition now being presented will provide us with a timely defense for national security and international engagement

[4408] This will make Forsvaret better adapted to the tasks and challenges it may face in the coming years

[4409] This means that the operational units are largely ready for action, are mobile and can be quickly deployed where needed

[4410] This will give us a defense that is more available to solve the tasks set by political authorities – both within and outside the country's borders

[4411] There is, however, reason to point out that the recommended operational structure in several areas lacks robustness, both in terms of personnel and material

[4412] Economic assumptions The MFU assumed a budget level, based on political guidelines, of NOK 29.7 billion/year in a long-term perspective

[4413] The present long-term budget proposal is based on a budget level of NOK 29.5 billion/year

[4414] The current year's budget level is 29.2 billion

[4415] was based on a framework of 123.5 billion for the four-year period (2002–

[4416] The actual allocation level as of 2004 is approximately 2.5 billion in total

[4417] All figures in 2004 kroner under these plans

[4418] Furthermore, the long-term budget proposal assumes the same optimistic assumptions for technological increases and operating cost growth as the MFU

[4419] In order to realize the structure on which the long-term proposal is based, it is assumed that the proposed rationalization and efficiency enhancement of the Ministry of Defence's logistics and support activities are followed up, while at the same time the recommended volume reductions in the operational structure are realized

[4420] Adaptation of operational structure The overall goal of the Chief of Defence's recommendation has been to undertake, to the greatest extent possible

[4421] reductions and streamlining within logistics and support activities while adapting these activities to a changed operational structure characterized by flexibility, accessibility and deployability

[4422] The intention has been to allocate a larger portion of resources to operational activities and material investments

[4423] The consequence of not realizing the proposed changes within logistics and support activities will be a reduced ability to modernize and streamline, and further cuts in operational structure

[4424] The operational structure proposed by the Long-term Proposal is a modern structure that is largely in line with the Chief of Defence's professional military advice, but with a lack of robustness in several areas, as previously mentioned

[4425] Nevertheless, it is pointed out that the challenges related to robustness cannot be solved satisfactorily by increasing the proportion of mobilization forces

[4426] The principled approach outlined is largely in line with the Chief of Defence's recommendations

[4427] Personnel – command and training system

[4428] When the focus is turned more towards operational issues, the 2003–2004 St.prop

[4429] No. 42 The further modernization of the Armed Forces in the period 2005–2008, which places demands on tangible, flexible and deployable forces of high quality, will place changed demands and conditions on everyone who serves in the Armed Forces

[4430] To meet these, the officer system, including the education system, must be changed and adapted to new framework conditions

[4431] It will be particularly important to strengthen the production of well-trained and experienced crews and managers at lower levels

[4432] New command arrangements, including a new arrangement for department commanders and enlisted personnel, contribute greatly to increasing continuity, skill levels, experience levels and maturity levels

[4433] This will contribute to increased safety during training, exercises and operations

[4434] Since international operations have become one of the Armed Forces' core tasks, the duty to give orders follows as a natural consequence

[4435] The obligation to order ensures access to personnel for international service and distributes the tasks and burdens that this service entails, but must be practiced in a predictable and personnel-friendly manner

[4436] In addition, the duty to order ensures that the expertise this provides is spread to the entire command corps

[4437] Together with the existing Professional Officers Act, the proposed changes to the officer system constitute a prerequisite for creating a relevant and effective defense

[4438] There is broad political and professional military agreement that the Norwegian armed forces should be based on conscription

[4439] Even when departments with a larger proportion of conscripts are gradually introduced, conscription will remain a pillar of the Armed Forces

[4440] However, it is absolutely crucial that the call-up force is adapted to the needs of the Defence if operating costs are to be kept at a reasonable level

[4441] This means that the call is adapted to the Armed Forces' manning needs and the provisions of the requirements catalogue to ensure the necessary recruitment of enlisted personnel and for officer training, as well as the recruitment basis for emergency preparedness contracts

[4442] The Chief of Defence is of the opinion that it is crucial for the future of conscription that it is modernised and adapted to the operational needs of the Armed Forces

[4443] An important part of the adaptation is that work must be done in a broad field to raise the status and recognition of those in military service

[4444] The Home Guard The long-term proposal mainly continues

[4445] for the Chief of Defence's proposal to implement a much-needed quality reform to adapt the Home Guard to a changed security policy picture

[4446] The main objective of the quality reform is to create a relevant HV where the Home Guard forces are given significantly better equipment, better training and more practice than today

[4447] This is achieved mainly by reducing the force volume and the number of districts

[4448] Today's tasks will still be solved, but in a more efficient way than today

[4449] According to the Chief of Defence's assessments, it is a prerequisite

[4450] that the resources to realize the quality reform are mainly obtained by reducing the current total force volume and the number of HV districts

[4451] Logistics and support activities The Chief of Defence's new logistics and support concept is intended as a central guideline for the development of the Armed Forces in the coming long-term period

[4452] concept aims to shift focus from managing a large, static and personnel-intensive logistics organization to a flexible and deployable operational logistics organization and a cost-effective support and management activity adapted to a modern and relevant operational structure

[4453] A number of measures are therefore also recommended that bring together the Armed Forces' activities and professional environments to a greater extent

[4454] This is being carried out to create strong expertise environments, synergies and cost efficiency

[4455] At the same time, a greater concentration of activities will be an important measure in terms of personnel policy in that it creates greater predictability and stability for individuals and their families

[4456] Allied cooperation In order to reduce the costs of both materiel investments and operations, continuous work should continue to find opportunities for division of labor and force integration with our allies

[4457] Increased levels of multinational material cooperation and joint logistics solutions will make our forces better able to operate together with allies and operations more cost-effective

[4458] In order to reduce the effect of technological cost increases and increased operating costs, as well as to ensure access to expertise, it is the Chief of Defence's assessment, in line with what the long-term proposal recommends, that cooperation with selected allies be intensified

[4459] National command structure

[4460] All future operations will take place in close cooperation between political and military authorities

[4461] This means that communication between political authorities, the Chief of Defence and the national command structure must be effective, secure and smooth

[4462] The Chief of Defence's ability to exercise general powers

[4463] No. 42 2003–

[4464] The further modernization of the Armed Forces in the period 2005–2008 must therefore be strengthened to meet future challenges, nationally and internationally

[4465] Cost-effective and flexible links between the national and allied command and force structure must be continuously developed

[4466] Once sufficient experience has been gathered from the existing command structure, it should undergo a comprehensive evaluation in its entirety, with the aim of making it more effective and modernizing it

[4467] Training and exercises

[4468] Another main challenge will be to ensure that the Armed Forces' units not only have sufficient and good equipment, but also that we have the level of training and activity that ensures the necessary training standard at all times

[4469] Modern training equipment and methods today make it possible to both educate and evaluate departments in a completely different and more realistic way than before

[4470] Simulators and other computer-assisted training at all levels will therefore be used to an increasing extent

[4471] The acquisition of increasingly complex military equipment and the requirement for high training standards require continuous, comprehensive training and exercise activities

[4472] Highly qualified personnel and jointly trained departments with a high training standard are today a prerequisite for flexibility, responsiveness and deployment capability both nationally and internationally

[4473] Large parts of the Armed Forces' investment portfolio during the planning period are tied up by investments in new frigates, new Skjold-class MTBs, helicopters for frigates and the coast guard, as well as the necessary upgrading and equipping of combat aircraft

[4474] This, together with reduced budget assumptions, means that other planned investments and modernizations must be postponed

[4475] This limits freedom of action, which is worrying

[4476] For the past ten years, no room has been found for renewal or investment in important capacities, such as renewal of national transport aircraft capacity and missile defense

[4477] The Chief of Defence, however, continues his recommendation regarding the need to acquire new modern combat aircraft over the next 10–15 years, but does not find room to finance this within the expected financial framework

[4478] The decision on procurement must be made no later than in connection with the processing of the next long-term period (2009–

[4479] Without extensive additional funding, the purchase of new combat aircraft will entail significant cuts in other parts of the operational structure

[4480] The army's materiel volume is proposed to be reduced in this proposition

[4481] In order for the proposed volume of materiel to be able to be defended, an absolutely necessary modernization and prioritization of the Army is assumed in the next long-term period (2009–

[4482] This long-term proposition proposes absolutely necessary measures to regain the balance between activity and resources, and at the same time shift the use of resources from logistics and support activities to operational operations and material investments

[4483] This will significantly improve the Armed Forces' ability to carry out its tasks

[4484] However, significant challenges still remain in finding space for the necessary modernization and renewal of the force structure

[4485] The long-term proposition is based on optimistic economic assumptions and ambitious savings targets to free up resources for operations and material investments

[4486] The Chief of Defence supports this facility, but is also concerned about the low total resource framework on which the long-term proposal is based

[4487] The proposed operational structure is not very robust in several areas, this particularly applies to the Army, which requires that the access to resources both within operational operations and material investments be maintained in the short and long term

[4488] If the availability of resources within operational activities weakens further, entire structural elements will probably have to be removed from the structure

[4489] Predictability and adequate resource allocation remain the most important factors for avoiding misinvestments and for the development of a modern, relevant and cost-effective defense
